The board ranks each team’s best; this shows every attempt.Submissions openStarter kitWhestBenchflopscopeHF datasetWhen can we know what a neural network does without running it?The ARC White-Box Estimation Challenge is a contest in compute-efficient mechanistic estimation. Given the weights of a neural network, can you predict its expected per-neuron activations more accurately than running it many times?The obvious way to learn how a model behaves is to run it many times and average what you observe. That works well when the behavior is common, cheap to elicit, and easy to sample. But when the behavior is rare, high-variance, or unlikely to appear in obvious test cases, brute-force testing can become an expensive way to learn very little.The ARC White-Box Estimation Challenge turns that question into a controlled benchmark. Participants receive randomly initialized ReLU MLPs and build executable estimators that predict each neuron's expected post-ReLU activation under standard-normal inputs.The goal is simple to state: beat comparable black-box sampling under a shared compute budget by using the network's weights. The strongest submissions may be Monte Carlo, white-box, hybrid, LLM-assisted, or something unexpected—the leaderboard will decide.TaskExecutable estimatorInputWeights + budgetOutputExpected activationsMetricFinal-layer MSELatestAnnouncementAug 23Phase 2 is live: new code restrictions, wider models, and a larger FLOP budget↗AnnouncementJun 18Phase 1 launched — deeper models, and increased prizes.↗All updates on the forum↗Official factsPrize pool$150,000 USD ARVTwo phases · $50K Phase 1 + $100K Phase 2 · places + algorithmicSubmissions openMay 28, 2026 · 00:00 UTCPhase 2 closesOct 17, 2026 · 23:59 UTCDaily limit10 per team · per UTC day, in Phase 2GraderCPU-only 1 core (2 vCPU) for your code · 7-core flopscope backend · 8 GB for your process · no networkHard cap120 s per MLPFinal rankingFresh private rerun of each team's up to two nominated submissions, per phaseFig. 1

The black-box path samples inputs, runs the network, and averages observed activations until the Monte Carlo mean stabilizes. The white-box path inspects W(1),…,W(L)W^{(1)}, \dots, W^{(L)}W(1),…,W(L) and propagates enough distributional information to predict the same means under the participant budget. The target is an organizers' high-budget Monte Carlo reference of approximately 3.36×10163.36 \times 10^{16}3.36×1016 FLOPs, compared with a participant budget of approximately 2.20×10122.20 \times 10^{12}2.20×1012 FLOPs per MLP—roughly a 15,000×15{,}000\times15,000× compute gap.Prizes$150K+Cash PrizesPrediction shape16 × 1024layers × width was 32 × 256Budget / MLP2.20e12FLOPsPhase 2 closesOct 172026 · 23:59 UTC01Why this starts with random networksThe benchmark isolates one hard part of white-box estimation: tracking how distributions move through nonlinear layers.White-box estimation for trained networks is the destination, not the starting line. Trained models introduce many confounders at once: data, optimization, learned structure, task semantics, and evaluation ambiguity. WhestBench begins with randomly initialized networks so participants can focus on the estimation problem in a simplified setting.The networks are synthetic, but the question is real — and it is a question about cost rather than possibility. Sampling gets there eventually on any network; what the benchmark measures is what the weights are worth once the budget is fixed.Random ReLU MLPs retain the same basic problem structure: each layer transforms a distribution, the ReLU nonlinearity reshapes it, and approximation error can accumulate with depth. The first challenge is to develop methods that work in this controlled setting; later work can ask how those methods adapt as networks acquire structure during training.The benchmark is controlled, but not trivial: the expected activation has no closed form for the full network, and sampling improves only slowly with more compute.Where the closed form stopsAt the first layer. Its pre-activations are Gaussian, so the ReLU mean is exact. Past it the distribution is a rectified Gaussian, neurons correlate as depth accumulates, and everything downstream is an approximation.02The taskFor each MLP, return a matrix of expected post-ReLU activation means.For each evaluation network MθM_\thetaMθ​, your estimator receives the MLP weights and a compute budget. It must return an L×nL \times nL×n matrix Y^\hat{Y}Y^. The grader runs your estimator against held-out MLPs and scores the returned activation matrix.03Compute model and constraintsThe competition is budgeted by analytical FLOPs, not by who owns the fastest machine.Compute is metered by flopscope, a NumPy-compatible interface that prices each operation analytically from its tensor shapes and operation kind. The count it reports for one network is FmF_mFm​, and this round that is the whole of CmC_mCm​, the cost charged against that network's budget BmB_mBm​.There is no second cost term because there is no computation outside the meter. NumPy is not installed on the grader — import numpy raises ModuleNotFoundError — and compiled kernels, foreign-function calls and subprocesses are prohibited rather than merely expensive. Your Python's job is to decide which flopscope operations to call.Time inside predict() that is not a flopscope operation is residual time: looping, indexing, bookkeeping, assembling arguments. It is capped at 400 ms per network, and crossing the cap fails that network through the zero-prediction fallback. The cap is what keeps the prohibition enforceable — it leaves no window in which meaningful computation could hide.Phase 1 priced residual time rather than prohibiting the computation in it: Cm=Fm+λRmC_m = F_m + \lambda R_mCm​=Fm​+λRm​ at λ=1011\lambda = 10^{11}λ=1011 FLOPs per second, so wall time and FLOPs traded against one another and CmC_mCm​ carried two terms. Phase 2 replaces that trade with a rule.import flopscope as flops
import flopscope.numpy as fnp

def predict(mlp, budget):
    mus = []
    mu = fnp.zeros(mlp.width)
    var = fnp.ones(mlp.width)

    for w in mlp.weights:
        mu_pre = w.T @ mu
        var_pre = (w * w).T @ var
        sigma_pre = fnp.sqrt(fnp.maximum(var_pre, 1e-12))
        alpha = mu_pre / sigma_pre
        mu = mu_pre * flops.stats.norm.cdf(alpha) + sigma_pre * flops.stats.norm.pdf(alpha)
        mus.append(mu)

    return fnp.stack(mus)Budget ruleStay within the per-MLP budget on every network. Over-budget runs, exceptions, invalid shapes, non-finite values, memory failures, or wall-clock guard failures receive the zero-prediction fallback for that MLP.Grader environmentYour code runs on one physical core (2 vCPUs); the remaining seven physical cores (14 vCPUs) run the flopscope backend and the evaluation harness. Submissions are CPU-only. Lower is better.All-layer MSE, averaged across all L×nL \times nL×n hidden activations, is reported as a secondary diagnostic. It helps reveal where approximation error accumulates across layers, but the primary score is the final-layer score.During each official phase, the grader evaluates submissions on a private suite of 100 randomly generated MLPs. Fifty contribute to live public feedback, while fifty are withheld until the phase closes. This keeps the leaderboard informative without making it too easy to overfit to visible scores.After each phase closes, each team's nominated submissions — up to two per phase, or your two highest-ranked public submissions if you nominate none — are rerun on a separate, freshly generated private test suite of new MLPs from the same distribution, using private seeds held out from both phases. Prize ranking is decided exclusively from this private rerun, not from the best public-leaderboard score observed during the competition.If leading submissions are statistically indistinguishable after the Private Re-evaluation, the Rules allow the Sponsor to generate additional MLPs from the same distribution for statistical disambiguation. If submissions remain tied after that, the tied ranks share the combined prize amounts for those positions.Public score vs. final prize rankThe public board helps you iterate. The final private rerun decides prize ranking.Failed-run fallbackIf a submission exceeds the budget, raises an exception, returns invalid shapes or non-finite values, exhausts memory, or trips an operational guard on a given MLP, the grader substitutes a zero prediction for that MLP and continues. No compute discount is applied to the fallback.Do not overfit the public boardThe final private suite uses different random MLPs. Strong submissions should generalize across the published generative distribution, not exploit visible leaderboard instances.05How to participateStart locally, validate the estimator contract, then submit a packaged tarball through AIcrowd.git clone https://github.com/AIcrowd/whest-starterkit.git

The current Rules specify $150,000 USD in total place-prize ARV — $50,000 in Phase 1 and $100,000 in Phase 2 — split across score-based and algorithmic contribution prizes. Each write-up maps to exactly one submission that was successfully graded in that phase.Deadlines — write-ups are due within a week of each phase closing:Aug 17 · 23:59Phase 1 algorithmic-contribution write-up deadlineOct 24 · 23:59Phase 2 algorithmic-contribution write-up deadlineAll times are UTC.The extra week is for writing onlyOnce a phase ends, its evaluator closes — you will not be able to make new submissions or re-grade anything for that phase. The submission you reference must already be successfully graded before the phase deadline (August 10 for Phase 1; October 17 for Phase 2).How ARC judgesGuidance from the Alignment Research Center (ARC)These prizes will be awarded at ARC's discretion to the method we think most improves our understanding of white-box estimation for random MLPs. We are most interested in "mechanistic" estimation methods, as discussed in our blog posts on competing with sampling and mechanistic estimation for wide random MLPs. We are less interested in methods that rely heavily on sampling, fine-tuned constants, careful performance optimization, and opaque LLM-optimized code (although clever sampling-based methods are of interest if they rely on interesting structural observations, and LLM-written code is of interest providing it can be deciphered).Technical writeups. The chance of a submission receiving an algorithmic contribution prize is greatly increased by the inclusion of a technical writeup explaining the algorithmic approach used and how it was developed. We will likely start by reading the technical writeup for the highest-scoring submissions, and award the prize to the submission where novel "mechanistic" ideas made the largest improvement to performance over previously-known methods.LLM usage. We are ultimately interested in the quality of the algorithmic contribution itself, regardless of how it was obtained, and LLM usage is encouraged. However, contestants should be fully transparent about the extent to which LLMs were used to generate code and/or portions of technical writeups. If contestants have significant uncertainty about how and why their code actually works, the relevant portions of the technical writeup should be appropriately hedged and/or labeled as guesswork (for example, "the LLM gave this explanation, which we did not validate/which we validated by ..."). If we notice unhedged, dubious claims, then we are likely to be more skeptical about the remaining content and may skip over submissions entirely.This guidance is also posted as ARC's guidelines post on the forum.Recognition beyond rankStrong submissions may be valuable even when they are not first on the leaderboard. Clear explanations, useful algorithmic ideas, helpful bug reports, and community contributions may be recognized according to the Rules and any later announcements on the Competition Site.Winning place-prize submissions are subject to verification and open-source release requirements described in the Rules. contests.title: RevenueCat Shipaton 2026
contests.description: Welcome to the RevenueCat Shipaton — the mobile hackathon that's all about shipping… a ton. At RevenueCat, we're all about supporting developers to build and monetize amazing apps. After the overwhelming success of last year's Shipaton, we're thrilled to announce the return of our global hackathon — and this year, we're going bigger than ever. This August and September, we're inviting builders from all corners of the globe to ship new apps and compete for over $740,000 in cash prizes and truly unique rewards — over $1 million worth of prizes in total. The challenge Ship a brand-new app to the App Store, Google Play Store, or — new this year — the Samsung Galaxy Store, between August 1st and September 30th, 2026. Integrate the RevenueCat SDK to power at least one in-app purchase or serve ads through RevenueCat Ads. Our goal is to give you that final push to ship that project you've had in the back of your mind but never took the time to get started. Note: Updates to previously released apps won't qualify - it's all about bringing something new to life! You can brainstorm, build, and post before August 1st, but your app must be released for the first time during the Shipaton window. Bigger and better Last year's Shipaton blew us away. Hundreds of new apps launched, thousands of #BuildInPublic posts went out, communities from Tokyo to Seoul to London hosted Shipaton IRL events, and winning teams ended up on stage in New York, accepting their Shippy trophies with their apps lighting up a Times Square billboard. Inspired by your amazing contributions, we've upped the ante for 2026: Over $740,000 in cash prizes — and growing as more sponsors join. Winning apps featured on giant billboards in Times Square. Flights to New York City for the Shippies red carpet award ceremony and RevenueCat's App Growth Annual conference. Press coverage for winners on 9to5Mac and 9to5Google. NEW: Investor exposure through the Shipaton Growth Fund. NEW: Shipaton Demo Day in Times Square. Every category winner who comes to New York will have the opportunity to demo their app to the public, meet potential users, and gather candid feedback beneath the winners’ Times Square billboards. Categories Grand Prize: Goes to the app that gains the most user traction and growth momentum during the event. We want to hear about what you've done post-release to push your app growth to the next level. [NEW] Next Gen Award: A student-only category for the best app submitted by active students — high school, university, bootcamp, campus dev club, anyone learning the craft. Judged on a video submission and open-source code, so no paid Apple or Google developer account is required. Open to students 13 and up. If you're under the age of majority where you live, a parent or guardian just needs to consent and agree to the rules on your behalf. Learn more on the Next Gen page. [NEW] Catvertising Award: Celebrates the most creative and effective use of RevenueCat Ads as a monetization method. We're looking for clever placements, smart integration with the rest of the revenue stack, and an experience users don't hate. [NEW] Best Game Award: For the best mobile game shipped during the event. We're looking for great gameplay, art direction, and a monetization fit that suits the genre. #BuildInPublic Award: For developers who share the most interesting development journey on social media. We're looking for compelling lessons learned or clever ideas that came from engaging with the community. HAMM Award (Help Apps Make Money): RevenueCat exists to "Help Apps Make More Money". This award goes to the project that designs the most robust and creative monetization strategy. RevenueCat Design Award: For the app that best represents the craft of app development — regardless of business potential. We're looking for innovative ideas and/or beautiful app design and animations. RevenueCat Peace Prize: Awarded to the project that provides the greatest social good. We're looking for apps with big benefits to communities or society at large. Conflict of Interest Award: A special category for RevenueCat employees and sponsors who couldn't resist joining the fun. No cash prizes, but a shot at glory. Influencer Award — Productivity: Christopher LawleyFor a polished productivity app that gives Apple power users one fast, focused place to save and retrieve reusable text snippets, documents, files, and images. Judges will consider product focus, speed, organization, intelligent features, and the quality of the overall design. Influencer Award — Nutrition & Healthy Eating: Abbey’s KitchenFor a flexible nutrition app inspired by Abbey’s Hunger Crushing Combo framework. Judges are looking for a compassionate, practical experience that helps users create more satisfying meals in real-life situations without calorie counting, macro tracking, or restrictive meal plans. Influencer Award — Yoga & Fitness: Simone ShariceFor a personalized wellness companion that answers, “What should I do today?” Judges will consider how effectively the app turns movement, Pilates, recovery, and other wellness needs into a clear, achievable daily plan without creating more information overload. Influencer Award — Career Coaching: Leadership HeatherFor an app that helps new managers practise difficult workplace conversations before the stakes are real. Judges are looking for realistic scenarios, useful feedback, confidence-building experiences, and active practice with situations such as feedback, boundaries, and saying no. Influencer Award — Gaming: Mr Lewis Blogs GamingFor a gaming bucket-list app that makes it easy to save games at the moment of discovery. Judges will consider how effectively users can organize, complete, rate, and share games, along with whether managing a backlog feels enjoyable rather than like another chore. Ship Kotlin Everywhere — JetBrainsRecognizes a creative, polished app built for both iOS and Android using Kotlin Multiplatform, Compose Multiplatform, or both. Judges will consider cross-platform quality, consistency, and effective use of Kotlin. Optional consideration may be given to useful build content and contributions to the Kotlin Multiplatform community. Most Viral App — NoiseAwarded to the app that captures the most attention in its market through high-quality, scalable content that converts into downloads. Judges will consider virality, whether the creative formats can be repeated at scale, and how clearly the content communicates the app’s value and addresses users’ needs. Best App for Galaxy — SamsungRecognizes a high-quality app published on the Galaxy Store and thoughtfully optimized for Samsung Galaxy users. Judges will consider the overall app experience and Galaxy-specific optimization, including foldable-device support, Samsung features, and device performance. Galaxy Store exclusivity may receive bonus consideration but is not required. Replit’s Idea to IncomeRecognizes a project that uses Replit to turn a new idea into a live, monetizing mobile app. Judges will primarily consider consistent week-over-week growth in revenue and transactions, supported by paying-user traction, product craft, visual design, and meaningful community engagement. Keep Them Coming Back Award — OneSignalRecognizes an app that uses OneSignal thoughtfully to bring users back. Judges will consider the quality and stability of the implementation, the value it adds to the user experience, and how creatively the app uses campaigns, push notifications, Journeys, or advanced messaging capabilities. The Growth Loop Award — LayersRecognizes a team that treats growth as a process of testing, measuring, learning, and improving. Judges will consider the clarity of the audience and growth hypothesis, how Layers was used to run and observe a focused experiment, whether the SDK was installed correctly, and what the team learned or would try next. Funnel Vision Award — StripeRecognizes a project that launches a web funnel using RevenueCat Funnels and Stripe. Judges will consider the qualifying web payment volume processed during the measurement period and whether the funnel is thoughtfully designed, functional, and effectively implemented. Prize structure You can find the official details of prizes at the bottom of this page, but here's how it all breaks down: Grand Prize Winner $100,000 Trip to New York City for the Shippies award ceremony and RevenueCat's App Growth Annual conference Custom Shippy trophy (presented live on stage!) App featured on a massive Times Square billboard Media spotlight on 9to5Mac and 9to5Google #BuildInPublic Category 1st Place: $30,000 + custom Shippy trophy + Times Square billboard feature + media spotlight + Trip to New York City for the Shippies award ceremony and RevenueCat's App Growth Annual conference 2nd Place: $20,000 3rd Place: $10,000 OneSignal's Keep Them Coming Back Award winner 1st Place: $25,000 + custom Shippy trophy + Times Square billboard feature + media spotlight 2nd Place: $15,000 3rd Place: $5,000 All Other Categories 1st Place: $20,000 + custom Shippy trophy + Times Square billboard feature + media spotlight 2nd Place: $10,000 3rd Place: $5,000 Times Square Demo Day for category winners Every Shipaton category winner who attends in person will have the opportunity to demo their winning app at Shipaton Demo Day in Times Square on October 22, 2026. Builders will rotate through shared demo pods between 10 AM and 6 PM. Participation is optional and subject to scheduling. Travel is included only for prizes that expressly list travel. Supported by the industry This year, our sponsors have shown up big. Huge thanks to Replit, OneSignal, JetBrains, Layers, Noise, Stripe, and Samsung for coming in as category sponsors for Shipaton 2026. And more sponsors are joining the fun all the time, which means bigger cash prizes and more additions to the Ship Kit. Ship Kit is back: Freebies for every Shipaton participant Ship Kit is your bundle of tools, credits, deals, and resources from our sponsors to help you build faster, launch better, and save a lot of money along the way. Some deals are while supplies last, so the sooner you register at the top of this page, the sooner you get access as Ship Kit starts to roll out. The #ShipatonSale If you have an app, tool, service, course, or template that could help Shipaton builders, run a sale for participants and share it with the #ShipatonSale hashtag. Submit it on the Shipaton website and we'll list community sales for everyone to find. Even if you're not competing, there are ways to support the builders who are. Shipaton IRL: Events near you We're excited to take Shipaton directly to developers around the world with Shipaton IRL. Last year, builders gathered in Tokyo, Seoul, London, St. Louis, Barcelona, Delhi, Vancouver, Warsaw, Skopje, and dozens of cities in between. This year, we want even more: kickoff parties, co-working days, weekend build sprints, launch-day meetups, and campus hackathons. Check out the events page regularly, as new events are being added all the time! Want to host a Shipaton event yourself? Apply now - we'd love to support you. Approved hosts get a Meetup-in-a-box with Shipaton swag, food vouchers, and organizer resources, and we'll promote your event to the massive Shipaton audience. Perfect for developer communities, hacker clubs, and student organizers planning campus events. Join the conversation on Discord! Shipaton isn't just about shipping code - it's about community. Whether you're brainstorming your first idea or prepping for launch day, the official Shipaton Discord is the place to connect, collaborate, and share the journey. Inside, you'll find fellow builders from around the world debugging code, running paywall experiments, discussing launch strategies, and more. Looking to form a team? Need quick feedback? Want to hang out with other shippers? You'll find it here. We've also created a dedicated #post-engagement-boost channel where you can share your YouTube videos, posts, and other #BuildInPublic content so other participants can like, comment, or share to help you reach a bigger audience. It's all about creating a positive, encouraging space where we lift each other - and help each other ship. Shipaton Livestreams Throughout the event, we'll host twice-a-week livestreams with expert guests, practical sessions, and live Q&A — so you're never building alone for two months. Come say hi 👋 and make the most of Shipaton! Ready, set, ship! Submissions open on August 1st and close on September 30th. Be sure to carefully review all submission requirements to ensure your app qualifies. We're beyond excited to see what the global builder community creates this year. Register today, and we'll keep you updated via the email address you use there. Let's get shipping!

contests.title: Global Innovation Build Challenge V2
contests.description: About the challenge Getting code to run has never been easier. Getting a system to actually work, at scale, under real constraints, is still hard. That gap is what this hackathon is about. Global Innovation Build Challenge (GIBC) V2 is a fully online, student-led international hackathon. GIBC V1 brought together 552 participants worldwide with backing from sponsors including NordVPN. V2 builds on that with three tracks, an international judging panel, and a larger sponsor lineup. Over the 10-week build period from July 11 to October 1, 2026, you can register at any time, build solo or in a team of up to 6, and submit to one of three tracks. Projects are reviewed by a panel of industry professionals and academic experts, with winners announced at a virtual closing ceremony on October 8, 2026. Track 01: TECH (Foundational LLM Development) Build and train a language model capped at 50 million parameters. You design the architecture, curate the data, and write the training loop. We want to see how much capability you can pull out of a deliberately small model. See the Rules page for exactly what the 50M cap includes and which benchmarks we score on. Example directions: a domain-specific assistant for legal or cryptographic text; a model optimized for on-device inference; a small generative model trained on a narrow technical corpus without touching a commercial API. Track 02: Applied (Medical Technology & Finance) Build a data-driven system on real, empirical datasets that solves a problem in healthcare or finance. This means predictive models, diagnostic pipelines, or automated financial systems, backed by data engineering that turns raw input into something a person could actually act on. Example directions: diagnostic software that processes device telemetry; analytics pipelines for pharmaceutical research; quantitative trading models driven by market indicators; automated risk scoring or fraud detection. All datasets must be public or de-identified, and prototypes must not be deployed on real patients or real money. See the Rules page. Track 03: Open (General Technical Invention) Build a functional prototype that shows technical novelty and cross-disciplinary engineering. Software, hardware, interactive media, generative systems, or any combination. No architectural limits and no resource constraints. Example directions: IoT-connected physical infrastructure; a tool that changes how you work day to day; a generative AI product; a full-stack application aimed at an environmental or community problem. Get started 1. Register on Devpost (July 11 to October 1)Sign up here on Devpost. You must be registered on Devpost to submit, even if you signed up on our website first. 2. Build solo or form a team (1 to 6 members)Work alone or assemble a team of up to 6. Once your team is set, pick the one track that fits what you want to build. Each team submits one project to one track. 3. Join the Discord (recommended)Join the official GIBC V2 Discord to find teammates, ask the organizers questions, and get announcements: https://discord.gg/4y6RghaSt5 4. Submit before the deadline (October 1, 11:45pm GMT+8)Submit all six required components on Devpost before the deadline. Late submissions are not reviewed.

contests.title: AWS Communication Developer Services (CDS) Agentic AI Partner Hackathon
contests.description: Calling all AWS Partners! We are inviting you to build the next wave of conversational solutions on AWS Communication Developer Services (CDS)! AWS CDS enables AWS Partners to help customers engage users at a global scale through AWS End User Messaging (EUM) which includes Rich Communication Services (RCS), Short Message Services (SMS), and WhatsApp. It also includes Amazon Simple Email Service (SES). AWS CDS is the infrastructure that powers messaging across Amazon.com, Amazon Cognito, SNS, and Amazon Connect. AWS CDS is often used for one-time passwords (OTP), notifications, and rules-based chatbots that follow rigid scripts. We challenge you to think beyond this. The future of customer engagement is conversational: reaching customers in the channel (i.e. email vs. RCS vs. WhatsApp) they prefer, picking up right where the last conversation left off, and using two-way communication so customers tell you directly what they want and share signals that improve your products and services. Picture omnichannel experiences where a conversation starts in one channel and completes an action in another: a prescription refill reminder via SMS that lets the patient find and schedule the nearest pharmacy pickup through RCS with a tap, then sends dosage instructions via email, all without leaving the messaging experience. Push the boundaries. Build agentic solutions where AWS CDS is the communications backbone, powered by AI such as Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Surprise us with your real customer and industry solutions! Why You Should Participate Innovate with AWS CDS. Get hands-on with AWS CDS combined with agentic AI powered by Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Solve Real Customer Problems. Create agentic solutions tied to customer and industry use cases that can scale across your customer base. Package your hackathon submission into a repeatable offering, list it on AWS Marketplace, and win AWS Specialist GTM and enablement support to accelerate real customer deals. Win Big. Compete for your share of $40,000 USD in cash prizes, in addition to an opportunity for a joint case study and 1:1 access to AWS Specialists to build and grow your AWS CDS practice and hackathon solution. Visibility for Your Organization. Winners will be announced via Devpost and the top winner will be offered a joint case study with AWS. Drive awareness and new leads to your practice. Direct Access to AWS Specialists. Join live webinars and weekly office hours to ask questions, get feedback, and shape the services roadmap. How to Get Started Now Brainstorm Your Idea. Think outside the box to improve customer communication experience through AWS CDS. Review the Tech Stack. Familiarize yourself with the AWS CDS services and how to pair them with agentic AI frameworks such as Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. See the Requirements below. Form Your Team (Optional). Find collaborators within the same AWS Partner organization who are excited to improve customer problems through AWS CDS. Diverse skillsets in development, architecture, and customer engagement can go a long way. Start Building. Stand up an RCS agent within 5 minutes to develop an entire solution, decide later to use RCS or phone numbers for each country you’re serving, and expand from there.

The IEEE OneAquaHealth Global Hackathon 2026 focuses on improving the sustainability and health of urban freshwater ecosystems by combining technology, citizen science, and the One Health approach. Urban aquatic environments are critical to biodiversity and human well-being but face increasing challenges due to urbanization, climate change, and limited monitoring capabilities. This challenge invites participants to build solutions that empower citizens and communities to actively contribute to environmental monitoring through intuitive tools and engaging experiences. Teams will explore ways to transform citizen-generated and environmental data into actionable insights that support researchers, policymakers, and local communities in making informed decisions. Participants are encouraged to leverage AI, data platforms, and digital health standards to improve the accuracy, reliability, and interoperability of ecosystem data while maintaining a human-centered approach. The hackathon also emphasizes raising awareness, fostering community engagement, and promoting long-term stewardship of urban water ecosystems through storytelling, gamification, and participatory design. By integrating environmental, climate, and citizen data, teams will help build early-warning systems, resilience tools, and decision-support platforms that strengthen ecosystem sustainability. Ultimately, this hackathon aims to advance the OneAquaHealth mission of connecting ecosystem health, biodiversity, and human well-being, driving innovation toward healthier communities and a more sustainable future. The hackathon aligns closely with the OneAquaHealth project, which is funded by the European Union. OneAquaHealth connects ecosystem health and human well-being through innovative tools for early detection of environmental risks. By combining biodiversity indicators, digital monitoring technologies, and community participation, OneAquaHealth helps identify how urban aquatic ecosystems respond to stressors. This holistic One Health approach supports evidence-based decisions for healthier, more resilient cities. contests.title: Build With AI: Basics
contests.description: Build With AI: Basics Build a working first draft of an app in an afternoon using AI best practices, with a set of reusable skills in your coding agent. Learn with a live build session, office hours, community, and a $2,500 prize pool, while creating something useful to your work or your life. About the challenge Devpost has launched a new kind of hackathon: shorter, built around learning, and open to join every month. Have you ever asked an AI to help you code something, only to watch it repeat a mistake you already fixed, forget a decision you made ten prompts ago, or hand back code that "works" but you can't explain? It happens to almost everyone who starts building with AI. Nobody showed you the basics. This hackathon does. You'll build a proof of concept: a small app that runs and does one thing end to end. To get there, you'll install the Devpost Learn Skill Pack, step-by-step guides that live inside your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or any agent that supports skills). The skills interview you about your idea, help you plan it before any code gets written, build it with you, and get it ready to submit. You'll finish with a running app, the plan that got you there, and a habit you can reuse on every project after this one. Why join Learn to plan before you build, by letting the AI interview you. It's the habit that keeps AI-built projects from turning into a mess. Try skills in your coding agent: reusable, step-by-step guides that work across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and others. Get help from real people: a live build session, office hours, and a live project review. Win a share of $2,500. First place takes $1,250 plus a feature in the Devpost newsletter and on Devpost's socials. Everyone who submits an eligible project gets a Devpost Learn badge. Get started You'll need Node.js and Git installed, a coding agent that supports skills, and an empty folder for your project. In your empty project folder, run npx skills add challengepost/learn-ai-basics --all -y Open your coding agent in that folder and say "run 1-start." It takes it from there. Join the Devpost Discord for questions, office hours, and other builders' projects. Register for the Live Build Session, Thursday, Oct 1 at 1:00 pm ET, where we run the whole process start to finish. “磐石·科学智能（AI for Science）实训营”由中国科学院物理所、自动化所、计算机网络信息中心和中国科学院大学主办，面向研究生、青年科研人员及优秀本科生，围绕科研智能体、AI4S方法论、科学模型和端到端科研闭环开展递进式训练。实训营旨在帮助学员建立系统认知，掌握AI-ready任务设计、模型实现与验证方法，并依托真实科研问题形成可持续推进的研究方案。同时沉淀模块化课程与教学资源，探索智能体原生科研人才培养模式，并推动优秀成果进一步发展为AI4S科研项目。

磐石·科学智能（AI for Science）实训营一、实训营简介人工智能辅助科学（AI for Science，AI4S）正由辅助数据处理的算法和工具，演进为深度参与文献调研、假设生成、实验设计、结果分析的新型科研系统，且将逐步从科研助手发展为可自主进化和探索科学任务的AI科学家。对于具有专业学科背景的科研人员而言，当前仍普遍存在知识与工具分散、系统认知不足、科学问题难以转化为可计算可评测的AI任务、通用智能体与专业科研场景适配不足，以及模型结果缺少可信验证和可复现保障等问题。如何将人工智能真正转化为解决科学问题的研究能力，是面向科技前沿和关键领域、增强研究生实践能力和创新能力需要回应的现实问题。“磐石·科学智能（AI for Science）实训营”由中国科学院物理研究所、中国科学院自动化研究所、中国科学院计算机网络信息中心、中国科学院大学主办，邀请AI4S（AI for Science）领域高水平专家和一流师资设计培训方案，联合开发课程，并提供案例支持。实训营依托磐石科学智能生态，主要面向全国希望将人工智能方法应用于科学研究的研究生、青年科研人员，以及具有良好数理基础、科研兴趣和自主学习能力的优秀本科生开放。实训营围绕科研智能体、AI4S科研方法论、科学模型和自驱动的端到端科研闭环设置课程，采用“前沿讲座——理论筑基——案例拆解——专题实训——问题研讨——场景参访——项目培育”的递进式培养模式，帮助学员建立系统化 AI4S认知，掌握将科学问题转化为 AI-ready 任务的基本方法，初步形成科研智能体与科学模型的设计、实现和验证能力，并围绕真实科研问题形成可继续推进的研究方案。在学员培养之外，实训营还将以课程建设为重要目标，探索面向智能体原生科研人才的 AI4S培养模式，形成覆盖科研智能体、AI4S科研方法论、科学模型和端到端科研闭环的模块化课程体系，沉淀教案、课件、实训脚本、代码数据、评价标准和助教手册等可复用教学资源，并建立真实问题牵引的课程迭代与科研培育机制。对于科学价值明确、研究条件基本具备且学员具有持续参与意愿的课题，实训营将通过双向选择、导师指导和持续项目跟进，推动部分学习成果进一步发展为 AI4S科研项目和实践成果。二、实训营特色注重 AI4S系统性认知与科研思维建立。实训营将围绕磐石科学基础大模型、科学数据、科研智能体、科研工具及计算——实验闭环等内容进行系统授课。帮助学员建立系统化 AI4S知识框架和将领域问题转化为数据条件明确、任务边界清晰、可计算、可评测的 AI-ready 任务的能力。构建智能体原生、实践嵌入式的实训体系。实训营将智能体的构建与应用贯穿于科研全流程，覆盖文献调研、假设生成、实验设计、数据处理与分析等关键环节。教学上采用“先构建最小可运行原型系统，再深入解析核心交互机制”的递进路径，帮助学员从实践中建立整体认知。课程系统讲授智能体架构、记忆机制、知识库管理及工具调用等核心技术原理，着重强化面向AI4S的科研实践能力。同时，注重培养学员在人机协同框架下开展复核审查的意识，提升对科学边界与模型局限性的判断力。建立真实问题牵引与科研培育机制。实训营课前征集真实 AI4S问题，学员报名时选择或自主提出问题，并通过课程学习、习题课和分组研讨逐步完善问题定义与技术路线。对于科学价值明确、研究基础条件已基本具备且学员具有持续参与意愿的课题，将通过双向选择机制匹配导师资源，并辅以持续性的项目跟踪指导，推动其进一步产出科学模型、科研智能体、科研工具或可复用工作流（含技能/MCP）等成果形式。推动学科交叉和科学智能生态构建。依托磐石科学智能生态和多学科科研体系，连接不同领域的科学问题、专业人才和技术能力，并引入科研平台、科技企业、算力及云服务等资源。通过研究所真实科研需求牵引课程教学，将科研任务、课程训练和青年人才培养贯通起来，促进领域知识、科学数据、模型算法、智能体工具和应用场景协同，使实训营同时成为
